steps.label: Go up to Bethel
steps.copy: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel. His household gives up their foreign gods, and Jacob buries them under the oak near Shechem.

steps.label: The altar at Bethel
steps.copy: He builds an altar where God had revealed himself when he fled from Esau.

steps.label: Named Israel again
steps.copy: God appears again, blesses him and confirms the name Israel and the promise of the land.

steps.label: Rachel dies
steps.copy: Still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin and is buried on the way to Bethlehem.

steps.label: Home to Isaac
steps.copy: Jacob comes to his father at Mamre, near Hebron. Isaac dies, and Esau and Jacob bury him.

set.note: 'Beyond the Jordan' (Genesis 50:10) usually means east of the river, which would make this a long way round. The site of Atad's threshing floor is unknown.

steps.label: Up from Egypt
steps.copy: Pharaoh's officials, Egypt's elders and Joseph's whole household go up with chariots and horsemen to bury Jacob.

steps.label: Mourning at Atad
steps.copy: Beyond the Jordan they mourn seven days, and the Canaanites name the place Abel-mizraim.

steps.label: Buried at Machpelah
steps.copy: His sons carry him into Canaan and bury him in the cave Abraham bought, just as he commanded.

steps.label: Back to Egypt
steps.copy: Joseph returns to Egypt with his brothers and everyone who went up with him.

set.note: Marah and Elim are debated sites; they are shown at the traditional locations on the Sinai coast.

steps.label: No water
steps.copy: From the Red Sea, Moses leads Israel into the wilderness of Shur. For three days they find no water.

steps.label: Bitter Marah
steps.copy: They reach Marah but cannot drink the water, for it is bitter, and the people grumble.

steps.label: The log
steps.copy: The Lord shows Moses a log that makes the water sweet. “I am the LORD who heals you.”

steps.label: Rest at Elim
steps.copy: They camp at Elim by twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees.

set.note: Exodus places the rock 'at Horeb' while the camp is at Rephidim; both sites are debated.

steps.label: Refused passage
steps.copy: Sihon king of the Amorites refuses to let Israel pass and comes out to fight them at Jahaz.

steps.label: Heshbon taken
steps.copy: Israel strikes Sihon, takes his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and settles in Heshbon, his city.

steps.label: Jazer taken
steps.copy: Spies are sent to Jazer, and Israel captures its villages.

steps.label: Og at Edrei
steps.copy: They go up the road to Bashan. Og comes out to fight at Edrei, and the Lord says, “Do not fear him.”

steps.label: Og defeated
steps.copy: They strike him down with his sons and his people and take his land.

set.note: Joshua 10:43 leaves Israel's camp at Gilgal before this campaign.

steps.label: Kings gather at Merom
steps.copy: Jabin king of Hazor calls the northern kings, and they camp together at the waters of Merom. The Lord tells Joshua not to be afraid.

steps.label: A sudden attack
steps.copy: Joshua comes against them suddenly by the waters of Merom, and the Lord gives them into Israel's hand.

steps.label: Hazor captured
steps.copy: He turns back and takes Hazor, the head of all those kingdoms.

steps.label: Hazor burned
steps.copy: Of all the cities on their mounds, Hazor alone is burned.

set.note: Judges calls Eglon's base the City of Palms, a name used for Jericho (Deuteronomy 34:3). Seirah's site is unknown.

steps.label: Bringing tribute
steps.copy: After eighteen years under Eglon of Moab, Israel cries out, and the Lord raises up Ehud, a left-handed man, who brings the tribute.

steps.label: The hidden sword
steps.copy: Ehud returns with a secret message for the king and drives his hidden sword into the very fat Eglon.

steps.label: Escape to Seirah
steps.copy: While the servants wait outside the locked doors, Ehud escapes past the idols to Seirah.

steps.label: The trumpet in Ephraim
steps.copy: He blows the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and Israel goes down after him.

steps.label: The fords seized
steps.copy: They seize the fords of the Jordan, strike ten thousand Moabites, and the land has rest eighty years.

set.note: Which Aroer is meant is uncertain. The Aroer by the Arnon is shown; another Aroer lay near Rabbah (Joshua 13:25).

steps.label: Made head at Mizpah
steps.copy: The elders of Gilead bring Jephthah back to lead them, and he repeats all his terms before the Lord at Mizpah.

steps.label: The Spirit comes
steps.copy: The Spirit of the Lord comes on him. He passes through Gilead and Manasseh, and makes a vow.

steps.label: Twenty cities struck
steps.copy: The Lord gives the Ammonites into his hand, from Aroer to the area of Minnith.

steps.label: Home to Mizpah
steps.copy: His only child, his daughter, comes out dancing with tambourines to meet him.

set.note: Micah's house is somewhere in the hill country of Ephraim; the spot is unknown. Mahaneh-dan was west of Kiriath-jearim (Judges 18:12).

steps.label: Spies sent out
steps.copy: With no land of its own yet, the tribe of Dan sends five men to explore.

steps.label: A priest at Micah's
steps.copy: They lodge at Micah's house and ask his Levite to inquire of God for them.

steps.label: Quiet Laish
steps.copy: They find Laish living quiet and secure, far from any help, and report back.

steps.label: Six hundred march
steps.copy: Six hundred armed men set out and camp at Kiriath-jearim, at the place called Mahaneh-dan.

steps.label: Micah's idols taken
steps.copy: In Ephraim they carry off Micah's carved image and his priest.

steps.label: Laish struck, renamed Dan
steps.copy: They strike the unsuspecting city, burn it, rebuild it and name it Dan.

set.note: Elkanah's town, Ramathaim-zophim (1 Samuel 1:1), is usually identified with Ramah.

steps.label: Up to Shiloh
steps.copy: Year after year Elkanah goes up to worship, and Hannah, who has no children, weeps and will not eat.

steps.label: Hannah prays
steps.copy: In deep distress she prays and vows: if the Lord gives her a son, she will give him to the Lord.

steps.label: Samuel is born
steps.copy: Back home at Ramah, she bears a son and names him Samuel.

steps.label: Given to the Lord
steps.copy: Once he is weaned, she brings the boy to the house of the Lord at Shiloh.

set.note: Bezek is usually placed at Khirbet Ibziq, northeast of Shechem.

steps.label: News at Gibeah
steps.copy: The people weep at Nahash's threat to Jabesh. The Spirit of God comes on Saul as he comes in from the field.

steps.label: Mustered at Bezek
steps.copy: Saul counts the army of Israel and Judah at Bezek.

steps.label: The dawn attack
steps.copy: In three companies they strike the Ammonites until the heat of the day.

steps.label: The kingdom renewed
steps.copy: All the people go to Gilgal and make Saul king before the Lord.

steps.label: The rocky pass
steps.copy: Saul stays on the outskirts of Gibeah while Jonathan and his armor-bearer slip toward the Philistine outpost between two crags.

steps.label: By many or by few
steps.copy: Jonathan says nothing can keep the Lord from saving, whether by many or by few.

steps.label: The climb
steps.copy: He climbs up on hands and feet, and the Philistines fall before him. The ground shakes.

steps.label: The Lord saves Israel
steps.copy: Saul's army joins in, and the Lord saves Israel that day.

steps.label: Sent to Bethlehem
steps.copy: “Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem.”

steps.label: The elders tremble
steps.copy: The town elders come trembling, and Samuel says he has come in peace to sacrifice.

steps.label: The youngest son
steps.copy: The Lord looks at the heart, not outward appearance. David, out tending the sheep, is sent for.

steps.label: Anointed with oil
steps.copy: From that day on, the Spirit of the Lord rushes upon David.

steps.label: Back to Ramah
steps.copy: Then Samuel sets out and goes home to Ramah.

steps.label: Bread at Nob
steps.copy: Ahimelech the priest gives David the consecrated bread.

steps.label: Goliath's sword
steps.copy: David takes the sword of Goliath, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod.

steps.label: Fleeing to Gath
steps.copy: He flees to Achish king of Gath, where he is recognized and becomes afraid.

steps.label: Feigning madness
steps.copy: He scratches on the doors of the gate and lets saliva run down his beard.

set.note: Mizpeh of Moab and the forest of Hereth are unknown sites; both are placed approximately.

steps.label: The cave of Adullam
steps.copy: David escapes to the cave, and his brothers and father's household come down to him.

steps.label: Four hundred gather
steps.copy: Everyone in distress, in debt or discontented gathers to him, and he becomes their leader.

steps.label: Parents to Moab
steps.copy: He asks the king of Moab to let his father and mother stay there.

steps.label: Into Judah
steps.copy: The prophet Gad tells him to leave the stronghold, so he goes to the forest of Hereth.

steps.label: Armies face off
steps.copy: The Philistines camp at Shunem and Israel at Gilboa. Saul is terrified, and the Lord does not answer him.

steps.label: Seeking a medium
steps.copy: Saul tells his servants to find him a woman who is a medium; there is one at Endor.

steps.label: By night, disguised
steps.copy: In disguise and by night, he goes to her, and Samuel appears.

steps.label: Samuel's word
steps.copy: Samuel says the Lord has torn the kingdom from Saul; tomorrow he and his sons will be with him.

steps.label: Back in the night
steps.copy: Saul collapses, eats what the woman prepares, and goes away that same night.

steps.label: David stays behind
steps.copy: In the spring, Joab and the army besiege Rabbah, but David stays in Jerusalem.

steps.label: Joab's message
steps.copy: Joab captures the royal city and sends for David to come and take Rabbah himself.

steps.label: Rabbah captured
steps.copy: David gathers the army, goes to Rabbah and takes it, and the king's crown is placed on his head.

steps.label: Home to Jerusalem
steps.copy: Then David and all the army return to Jerusalem.

steps.label: Israel follows Sheba
steps.copy: Sheba blows a trumpet and Israel deserts David, but Judah stays with its king all the way to Jerusalem.

steps.label: At the great stone
steps.copy: Joab's men set out after Sheba. At the great stone in Gibeon, Joab kills Amasa.

steps.label: Through all Israel
steps.copy: Sheba passes through all the tribes to Abel-beth-maacah, and Joab builds a siege ramp against it.

steps.label: A wise woman
steps.copy: She persuades the city, and Sheba's head is thrown over the wall to Joab.

steps.label: Back to the king
steps.copy: Joab blows the trumpet and returns to the king in Jerusalem.

set.note: 1 Kings 5:9 says the logs were floated in rafts to the place Solomon would name; 2 Chronicles 2:16 names it as Joppa.

steps.label: Cedars of Lebanon
steps.copy: Solomon asks Hiram for cedar, for no one can cut timber like the Sidonians.

steps.label: Laborers in relays
steps.copy: Thirty thousand men go to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month.

steps.label: Floated by sea
steps.copy: Hiram's men bring the logs down to the sea and float them in rafts.

steps.label: Stone and timber
steps.copy: The builders prepare the timber and great cut stones for the house of the Lord.

steps.label: A room for the prophet
steps.copy: A woman of Shunem and her husband build a small upper room for Elisha.

steps.label: The child dies
steps.copy: The son promised to her sits on her lap until noon, and then he dies.

steps.label: Riding to Carmel
steps.copy: She saddles the donkey and rides to the man of God at Mount Carmel.

steps.label: The boy raised
steps.copy: Back at the house, the child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes.
